decisions.statement: A running client watches the settings file that client was launched with.
A file's name stops describing that file's contents once the body is written again.
A hook's registration is read once, when the client starts.
Every settings file a running process names is read.
The document is read once and every file is written from that one reading.
The per-spawn keys a file has are carried into the file replacing that file.
A file already with the body that would be written is left alone.
The digest in a file's name is left as the digest is.
A file that will not read is reported rather than written.
Every file is acted on rather than the run stopping at the first that will not read.
Reading no live settings file at all is a data refusal.
Nothing here stops a seat or a client.
Nothing here writes the settings document.
A run that stopped part way is refused naming each file written before it stopped.
A run that stopped before writing a file is refused as the fault alone.

definition: the command rewriting each running seat's settings file from the document as it now is
